---
title: "Quiz 3"
author: "Amanda Mae Woodward"
date: "2025-10-30"
output: html_document
---
1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
library(readr)
spotDat <- read_csv("spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
View(spotDat)
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist))+geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()
```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))+scale_fill_brewer(palette= "Greens")
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+geom_bar()+theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
spotWide<- spotDat |> pivot_wider(id_cols=c("artist","tempo","song", "popularity", "danceability"), names_from="genre", values_from="genre", values_fn=list) 

```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
spotLong<- spotWide |> pivot_longer(cols=c(colnames(spotWide)[6:64]), names_to="genres", values_to="song genre")
```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
spotGraph<- ggplot(spotDat, aes(artist, fill=genre))+ geom_bar()+theme((axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)))
spotGraph+facet_wrap(~genre)
```

9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability))+geom_point(shape=4)+theme_bw()
```

10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+geom_point(shape=4)+theme_dark()
```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotDat, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity))+geom_point(shape=4)+scale_color_viridis(discrete=FALSE, option="plasma")
```
